title: Prompt Variant Fabricator — personal experiment log
content:
Personal tinkering log — fabricator approach to prompt variants

High-level intent:
- Build a small, reusable library of prompt "variants" that can be programmatically composed (anchors + splice points) to test stability across model size and quantization.
- Capture failure patterns and lightweight heuristics for choosing variant families per task (classification, summarization, instruction-following).

Design notes / terminology (working):
- Anchor: an instruction block intended to set role + constraints (short, 1–3 sentences).
- Splice: a slot where examples or context are inserted (few-shot exemplars or dynamic context).
- Lattice: the combinatorial grid of anchor x splice x priming temperature.
- Oracle anchor: an anchor crafted to reduce ambiguity (explicit yes/no boundaries).
- Drift: when exemplar ordering or tokenization causes response variance over time.

Quick experiments (chronological):
1) Experiment A — "oracle anchor" + 3-shot labelled examples - Prompt: [Anchor: "You are a strict code reviewer. Only list issues and line numbers."] + 3-shot exemplars (good/bad) + request - Model: open-7b-v2-quant - Observed: model occasionally adds suggestions that are stylistic rather than actionable; hallucinated line numbers when code shorter than examples. - Hypothesis: anchor too permissive on "only list"; exemplar length bias causes invented line numbers. - Mitigation tried: add explicit token-length guard ("if no line numbers, say 'no issues found'"). Partial improvement but still inconsistent on short inputs.

2) Experiment B — "anchoring splices" for summarization (few-shot vs zero-shot) - Anchor variant 1: "Summarize in 2–3 bullet points focusing on cause and impact." - Anchor variant 2: "Write 1–2 sentences suitable for a product changelog." - Few-shot set: 2 examples each, one long paragraph, one short paragraph. - Observed: few-shot examples force style but also introduce hallucinated "suggested actions" not present in source; zero-shot with very explicit anchor produced cleaner, shorter output. - Note: might be dataset effect (our examples included action items). Need to audit exemplars for leakage.

3) Experiment C — role swap + temperature sweep for conversational moderation - Roles: "safety analyst" vs "policy enforcer" - Temperature: 0.0, 0.2, 0.6 - Observed: at 0.0 both roles give similar conservative responses; at 0.6 "policy enforcer" tended to add punitive language. - Fail cases: subtle bias introduced by role wording ("enforcer" triggers punitive tone).

Representative prompt templates (stubs):
- TEMPLATE_A (classification):
  Anchor: "You are a precise classifier. Only output a single label from the set {POSITIVE, NEGATIVE, NEUTRAL}. Do not provide explanation unless asked."
  Splice: one or more short labeled examples (label <TAB> text)
  Post: "Classify: <input>"

- TEMPLATE_B (structured extraction):
  Anchor: "Extract the following fields in JSON: {name, date, amount}. If a field is missing, put null. Output only valid JSON."
  Splice: optional example(s) showing edge cases (ambiguous dates, currency symbols)

- TEMPLATE_C (few-shot code critique):
  Anchor: "You are a careful reviewer. For each issue, list: severity|line-range|explanation (one-sentence)."
  Splice: 2 examples where one includes no issues (to enforce explicit 'no issues')

Failure modes catalog (short):
- Label collapse: model repeats same label across unrelated inputs when exemplars unbalanced.
- Overfitting to exemplar phrasing: model parrots exemplar wording instead of generalizing.
- Hallucinated structural tokens: inventing line numbers, JSON keys, or amounts when unsure.
- Tone drift: role wording amplifies undesired phrasing ("enforcer" -> punitive).

Diagnostic checklist (to run when model misbehaves):
- Are exemplars biased/unbalanced? (yes/no)
- Exemplar lengths similar to target inputs? (yes/no)
- Anchor contains implicit instructions (e.g., "be helpful") that conflict?
- Temperature and top-p consistent with intent (0–0.2 for deterministic tasks)
- Is tokenization slicing examples into different token count distributions (quantized models more sensitive)?

Notes on exemplar curation:
- Prefer minimal exemplar wording — avoid extra commentary (no "note:" lines).
- Include explicit negative examples ("no issues found") to reduce hallucinated constructs.
- Rotate exemplar ordering during batch eval to detect ordering sensitivity.

Mini-protocol for building a variant family (practical steps):
1) Choose task and desired output form (label, JSON, bullet list).
2) Draft 3 anchor variants (conservative / neutral / permissive).
3) Create 4 exemplars per family: 2 positive examples, 1 ambiguous, 1 negative (no-output)
4) Run cross-product of anchors x exemplar-sets x temp(0,0.2) x model-size(small,med)
5) Collect metrics: label accuracy, hallucination rate (binary), length distribution, tone score (heuristic)
6) Inspect top 20 failure cases manually and add targeted anchor text where needed

Hypotheses to test (next iteration):
- H1: adding an explicit "if uncertain, say "can't determine''" line in anchor reduces hallucinated numbers by >60%
- H2: exemplar balancing (equal counts per label) reduces label collapse but may increase variance — measure tradeoff
- H3: short, explicit anchors beat long narrative anchors for structured-output tasks on quantized models

Ad-hoc notes / scratch points:
- Try replacing the word "reviewer" with "validator" in code-critique anchor to see if punitive tone drops.
- For summarization, test a "signal sentence" exemplar where we tag sentences to highlight causality vs outcomes.
- Add a tiny eval harness in prompt-lib: randomize exemplar order, log deterministic seed, store prompt snapshot (important for regression) — link to PR (above).

Outstanding TODOs:
- [ ] curate a 20-example exemplar bank for classification (balanced) — assign to Luis
- [ ] implement ordering-randomization in eval harness (PR reviewer: Priya)
- [ ] short audit of tokenization effects on open-7b-v2-quant (Theo)
- [ ] draft a one-pager for SRE on how to embed deterministic anchors into reroute fallbacks

Slack notes / quick refs:
- See thread slack:#prompt-hackers (ts:1623456789) for earlier tone experiments.
- Linear ticket LIN-3456 tracks the exemplar-rotation task.

Random musings (untagged):
- Could we encode a micro-protocol in a comment token (e.g., "// anchor_id: A12") that we append to prompts for better provenance without exposing customers? Might help tracebacks in logs.
- Thinking about an "anchor fingerprint" hash to detect accidental changes during CI — small and fast.

End of log for now.

-- a.c.
